subject: Project Beacon: customer-facing stabilization plan and exec sync
messages:
From: Alex Hwang <alex.hwang@finova.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.com
Cc: priya@finova.com
Date: 2028-03-09T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Project Beacon - checkout failures / throughput spike

David —

We started seeing failures in checkout starting ~07:45 PT. Metrics from our side: p95 latency jumped to ~1.6s (baseline ~120ms), successful throughput down ~40%, and error rate spiked to 6.8% (mainly 5xx from the inference endpoint). This is affecting ~12% of our live transactions and we've had two merchant timeouts.

Our SREs captured sample traces and request ids; attached a CSV with logs and a short dashboard clip. We need an immediate plan and an exec-level update for our COO — they're asking what Redwood is doing and ETA to return to normal.

Can you put together a stabilization plan and set a call for an exec sync? We need:
- short-term mitigation (routing, retries, throttling)
- owners for customer comms
- timeline for rollback/patch if needed

Thanks — please confirm receipt.

Alex Hwang
Head of Platform Reliability, Finova
[Attachment: finova_error_logs_0309.csv]

From: david.kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hwang <alex.hwang@finova.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-09T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Project Beacon - checkout failures / throughput spike

Alex —

Received and sorry for the customer impact. We're standing up a focused stabilization bridge now. Attaching an initial action plan (v0) and a short runbook we'll execute immediately. High-level commitments:

1) Immediate mitigation (next 30–90 minutes):
   - Route traffic away from the affected inference pool to our warmed fallback fleet (estimated +25% capacity)
   - Increase client-side retry budget and reduce TTL for prefix cache on eligible routes
   - Apply routing throttles to reduce amplification from noisy clients

2) Triage & fix (1–6 hours):
   - Deep log aggregation and KV cache validation (owner: karthik)
   - Hotfix to routing policy if misrouting identified (owner: lauren)

3) Customer comms & exec sync (now +45m):
   - Marissa will prepare an exec-facing status note and join you on a 30-minute bridge at 10:00 PT

We've looped in the right owners. We'll send a short customer-facing status in 20 minutes and hold the 10:00 PT bridge.

[Attachment: beacon_action_plan_v1.pdf]

— David Kim
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-09T09:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Project Beacon - troubleshooting notes

Quick triage notes from infra:

- Initial traces indicate a burst of requests with long context lengths correlated to the spike; KV cache miss ratio jumped ~3x at 07:44–07:55.
- Some backend allocation churn reported on pool-redwood-46; we saw a transient rebalancing event at 07:49 that coincides with increased tail latency.

Immediate actions I'm taking now:
- Force-invalidate prefix cache for affected routes to avoid stale KV lookups (will take ~60s to propagate)
- Temporarily pin Finova traffic to fallback fleet (non-preemptible nodes) to stabilize latency while we analyze stateful caches
- Aggregating sample request ids to correlate traces (writing to /tmp/finova-traces-0309)

I'll post console links and the first set of trace ids in the bridge. If the cache invalidation drops error rate, we can keep pinned routing for 2–4 hours and then slowly shift back.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: monica.patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.com, Alex Hwang <alex.hwang@finova.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-09T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Status update for Finova execs

Alex / David —

Quick customer update that I shared with Finova's platform leadership at 10:45 PT:
- Root cause under investigation; current hypothesis is cache invalidation + fleet rebalancing causing tail latency and 5xxs
- Mitigation applied: traffic pinned to fallback fleet; observed drop in error rate from 6.8% -> 1.2% within 20 minutes
- Short-term ETA: continue monitoring, expected stabilization in 1–3 hours barring further anomalies

Finova asked for an exec note that summarizes impact and our plan. Marissa will send the formal note; I'm on call for any escalation.

— Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: david.kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hwang <alex.hwang@finova.com>, priya@finova.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-09T15:52:00-07:00
Subject: Project Beacon — stabilization summary and next steps

Alex / Priya —

Summary of where we are after the stabilization bridge:

What happened (short):
- At ~07:45 PT a combination of an elevated long-context request burst and an internal pool rebalancing event increased KV-cache miss ratio and created tail latency that propagated to 5xx responses for a subset of requests.

What we did (actions completed):
- Pinned traffic to a warmed fallback fleet to reduce tail latency (completed by 09:05 PT)
- Performed prefix cache invalidation for affected routes (09:10 PT)
- Applied conservative routing throttles and increased client retry budget to reduce surface area of failing calls (09:20 PT)

Immediate impact observed:
- Error rate reduced from 6.8% -> 0.9% over the first hour
- p95 latency returned to ~210ms (still above baseline while we finish cache repopulation)

Next steps and owners:
- Short-term: keep pinned routing for up to 4 hours while we validate KV cache repopulation and run an automated canary (owner: karthik)
- Medium-term: post-mortem and mitigation patch to routing logic to prevent simultaneous rebalancing + long-context amplification (owner: lauren) — ETA 48 hours
- Customer comms: Marissa to send an exec-friendly incident note and coordinate a follow-up in 24 hours

We will provide a detailed post-mortem and a list of tactical and systemic changes within 48 hours. I've attached the action plan and the logs we reviewed. Please let me know any immediate questions — standing by on the bridge if you'd like to reopen.

Thanks for your patience and the quick cooperation from the Finova SREs.

— David Kim
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Attachments: beacon_action_plan_v1.pdf, latency_trends_0309.png]
